advisory.title: Possible signature replay in Action Mailbox Mailgun ingress
advisory.description:
### Impact

The Action Mailbox Mailgun ingress authenticates a request with an HMAC of the
`timestamp` and `token` parameters concatenated without a separator, and
`ActionMailbox::Ingresses::Mailgun::InboundEmailsController::Authenticator#recent?`
rejects only timestamps more than 2 minutes in the past. Because the signature
does not fix the boundary between the two values, a captured signed request
can be presented with a timestamp far in the future, which the ingress then
accepts indefinitely. An attacker who obtains one signed Mailgun webhook
request, but not the signing key, could submit arbitrary inbound email that
Action Mailbox processes as genuine, possibly leading to forged messages
attributed to the sender of the attacker's choosing.

Applications that receive inbound email through the Action Mailbox Mailgun
ingress are affected.

### Details

The fixed releases also reject a Mailgun request whose timestamp is more than
2 minutes ahead of the server's clock, as they already did for one more than 2
minutes behind it. An application whose clock runs more than 2 minutes behind
Mailgun's will now reject genuine webhooks and should synchronize its clock.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c3a295c5c22266e8ec4d0e664e6923a299235e7a.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/4aa2ec66822bc4eb8b341a0608f1c90a3e371a34.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[davutselcuk](https://hackerone.com/davutselcuk).

advisory.title: Possible restoration of destroyed sessions in Action Dispatch CacheStore
advisory.description:
### Impact

`ActionDispatch::Session::CacheStore` writes a session back to the cache at
the end of each request that loaded it, without checking that the session's
cache entry still exists. When a concurrent request destroys the session,
through `reset_session` on logout or by deleting its cache entry on the
server, a request that loaded the session earlier and finishes later restores
it under its original session ID. Logout and server-side revocation could
therefore fail to end a session, and an attacker who holds a stolen session
cookie could keep that session valid across the victim's logout.

Applications that use `config.session_store :cache_store` are affected, with
any cache backend. `ActionDispatch::Session::CookieStore` is not affected, nor
is `ActionDispatch::Session::MemCacheStore` with Dalli 4.0.0 or later, whose
session store does not write back a session that was deleted.

### Details

The fixed releases record which session a request loaded and skip the write
when that session's cache entry no longer exists. Changes that such a request
makes to the destroyed session are discarded, and Rack logs a warning that the
session could not be saved. Each request that writes back a session it loaded
makes one additional cache read.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/d479192cf88a8b30a335a8bc25188a2d8e0f8d9f.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/5bb5ec66ed8faaf590ffe1222d7a5eb6e9d050f5.patch

### Credit

Found by the team during internal code review.

advisory.title: Missing SameSite attribute on session cookies from Action Pack session stores
advisory.description:
### Impact

Action Pack session stores other than `ActionDispatch::Session::CookieStore`
(`CacheStore`, `MemCacheStore`, and third-party stores built on
`AbstractStore`, `AbstractSecureStore` or the session mixins) write the
session cookie without a `SameSite` attribute, regardless of
`config.action_dispatch.cookies_same_site_protection`, which defaults to
`:lax`. Only `CookieStore` applies the configured policy. In browsers that do
not treat a cookie without the attribute as `SameSite=Lax`, a cross-site
request could carry the session cookie, possibly leading to cross-site request
forgery against actions that do not verify an authenticity token, such as
those of API-only applications.

Applications are affected when they use a session store other than
`CookieStore` and do not pass `same_site:` to `config.session_store`.

### Details

In the fixed releases, every session store sets the session cookie's
`SameSite` attribute from `cookies_same_site_protection` when its options have
no `:same_site` key. An explicit `same_site:` option, including
`same_site: nil`, and a `:same_site` value in a store's `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`
still take precedence.

### Workarounds

Pass `same_site:` when configuring the session store, for example
`config.session_store :cache_store, same_site: :lax`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/2d9f502df941e31ce9bad0e846564f49396bed46.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/f2392996be723708271a8d30bfcf0edc221e53ef.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[tjvc](https://hackerone.com/tjvc).

advisory.title: Possible cache poisoning in Action Pack content negotiation
advisory.description:
### Impact

Action Pack negotiates the format of a rendered response from the `Accept`,
`X-Requested-With` and, for XHR requests without `Accept`, `Content-Type`
request headers, but `ActionController::Rendering#_set_vary_header` adds
`Vary: Accept` only when the request carries a usable `Accept` header and the
response has no `Vary` header yet. A response to a request without `Accept`,
or to an XHR request, therefore omits the headers that selected its
representation, and a response whose `Vary` the application set before
rendering (for example `Vary: Accept-Language`) never gains `Accept`. A shared
cache that honours `Vary` could store such a response and serve it to later
clients that request a different representation, possibly leading to cache
poisoning in which visitors receive, until the entry expires, a page without
its layout or HTML in place of JSON. The attacker cannot choose the content of
the response.

Applications that render negotiated responses from actions marked `public`
(for example with `expires_in ..., public: true`) behind a shared cache that
honours `Vary`, such as Thruster or `Rack::Cache`, are affected.

### Details

In the fixed releases, a rendered response whose format is not given by the
URL lists `Accept` and `X-Requested-With` in `Vary`, and also `Content-Type`
for an XHR request without `Accept`; when
`config.action_dispatch.ignore_accept_header` is enabled, it lists only
`X-Requested-With`. These fields are appended to an existing `Vary` value
rather than skipped, and `Vary: *` is left unchanged. Shared caches can store
more variants of such responses than before. See the Action Pack CHANGELOG for
details.

### Workarounds

Set `Vary: Accept, X-Requested-With` on negotiated responses in the
application, for example in an `after_action`, or do not mark negotiated
responses `public`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/7a955ca36779938267c93902c47d1f55bab99b4b.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/b58c107abe9c1f10c1d6a4941402c60e4dc4742c.patch

### Credit

This issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-7GHGLQGO,
ANT-2026-5MT6C2R3).

advisory.title: Possible DoS vulnerability in Action Controller Live streaming
advisory.description:
### Impact

`ActionController::Live::Buffer#close` pushes its end-of-stream marker onto
the response's bounded queue while it holds the buffer's monitor. When the
client has stopped reading and the queue is full, the push blocks, and
`Buffer#abort`, which runs when the client disconnects or a write times out,
waits indefinitely for the same monitor. Each such response could permanently
hold a web server thread and its `ActionController::Live` thread, possibly
resulting in a DoS vulnerability through thread exhaustion.

Applications that stream responses with `ActionController::Live`, including
`send_stream`, are affected. Applications that serve large files through
Active Storage proxy mode are exposed to unauthenticated clients.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/ccbfc09690fef05fdd2a9969c917a71b92cc98fc.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/27ad18ed5900dee28ba20e9c6fc718ff751fa215.patch

### Credit

This issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-LDFW5N2T).

advisory.title: Possible Strong Parameters bypass in Parameters#each_key in Action Pack
advisory.description:
### Impact

`ActionController::Parameters#each_key` delegates to the internal
`ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess` that holds the request parameters,
so when called with a block it returns that hash instead of the `Parameters`
instance. The hash does not respond to `permitted?`, so Active Model mass
assignment (`new`, `assign_attributes`, `update`) accepts it without raising
`ActiveModel::ForbiddenAttributesError`. An application that passes the return
value of `each_key` to mass assignment could allow a remote, unauthenticated
attacker to set attributes that the application does not permit, such as an
authorization flag.

This is an incomplete fix of
[CVE-2020-8164](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8727-m6gj-mc37), which made
`each`, `each_pair` and `each_value` return the `Parameters` instance but left
`each_key` delegated.

### Details

The fixed releases define `Parameters#each_key` to yield each key and return
the `Parameters` instance when given a block, as `each`, `each_pair` and
`each_value` do, and to return an `Enumerator` without one. Code that used the
return value of `each_key` as a hash now receives the `Parameters` instance,
which mass assignment rejects unless it is permitted.

### Affected applications

An application is affected if it passes the return value of
`ActionController::Parameters#each_key`, called with a block, to mass
assignment. Rails itself makes no such call.

### Workarounds

Do not use the return value of `each_key`. Call it for its block only, and
pass the permitted `Parameters` instance to mass assignment.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/8ba746e0a786458c281060823f2ccc5c5f6312ac.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/2fc8838300133931e19eed3ea6cee76a7e83f19c.patch

### Versions affected

- actionpack < 8.0.5.2
- actionpack >= 8.1, < 8.1.4.1

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[smlee](https://hackerone.com/smlee).

advisory.title: Possible sensitive session information leak in Active Storage proxy mode
advisory.description:
### Impact

When `ActionDispatch::Cookies` reads a signed or encrypted cookie that was
written under a rotated secret (`config.action_dispatch.cookies_rotations`) or
in the format that a `:hybrid` cookie serializer migrates from, it writes the
cookie back to the response in the current format, and that write ignores
`request.session_options[:skip]`. `ActiveStorage::DisableSession` relies on
that option to keep the session cookie off the public, immutable responses of
the Active Storage proxy controllers, but those controllers still load the
session, so a request carrying an old-format session cookie could receive the
rewritten session cookie in `Set-Cookie` on a cacheable response. A shared
cache that stores such a response together with its `Set-Cookie` header could
then serve one user's session to later requesters of the same URL, or serve an
attacker's session to other users.

Applications are affected when they serve Active Storage files through the
proxy controllers, have a cookie rotation or a `:hybrid` serializer migration
configured, and run behind a cache that stores `Set-Cookie` on public
responses. This is a path around the fix for
[CVE-2024-26144](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8h22-8cf7-hq6g).

### Details

In the fixed releases, a response that skips the session leaves an old-format
signed or encrypted cookie unchanged, and the next request that does not skip
the session upgrades it. An application that skips the session on every
request no longer upgrades its signed or encrypted cookies. Cookies that the
application sets explicitly are still written. See the Action Pack CHANGELOG.

### Workarounds

Configure caching proxies not to store responses that carry a `Set-Cookie`
header, or complete the cookie rotation or serializer migration and remove it
from the configuration.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/849a6c30eacbb6ca4722132f43c4333a93188556.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/0e6cf8faa89caf4c64311d35ca2bc88c1458d4e3.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[flashmyname](https://hackerone.com/flashmyname).

advisory.title: Rails has a possible XSS vulnerability in its Action View tag helpers
advisory.description:
### Impact
When a blank string is used as an HTML attribute name in Action View tag helpers,
the attribute escaping is bypassed, producing malformed HTML.
A carefully crafted attribute value could then be misinterpreted by the browser as a separate attribute name,
possibly leading to XSS. Applications that allow users to specify custom HTML attributes are affected.

### Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View text helpers
advisory.description:
### Impact

With the HTML5 sanitizer (`Rails::HTML5::Sanitizer`, the default vendor on
CRuby for applications using `load_defaults 7.1` or later), Nokogiri before
1.19.5 serializes `<` and `>` unescaped inside attribute values. The Action
View text helpers `highlight` and `simple_format` sanitize their input and
then process the resulting HTML as a string: `highlight` splits it on tag
boundaries to insert matches, and `simple_format` splits it into paragraphs on
blank lines. An unescaped `>` or a blank line inside an attribute value could
cause markup in that value, which the sanitizer left inert, to be emitted as
live elements in the helper's `html_safe` output, possibly leading to XSS.
Applications that use the HTML5 sanitizer and pass untrusted text to
`highlight`, or to `simple_format` with `html_options`, are affected.

### Details

The fixed releases require rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.2 or later, which requires
Loofah 2.25.3 and Nokogiri 1.19.5. With these versions, the HTML5 sanitizer
escapes `<` and `>` in attribute values as `<` and `>`, as the HTML4
sanitizer already does. The parsed DOM is unchanged, but code or tests that
compare sanitized HTML as a string may see the new serialization.

### Workarounds

Upgrade Nokogiri to 1.19.5 or later; the escaping is in its HTML5 serializer,
so no Rails upgrade is needed. Alternatively, use the HTML4 sanitizer by
setting `config.action_view.sanitizer_vendor = Rails::HTML4::Sanitizer`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/adc3a32d4abea77ed3aacf6f5fb71cfc005bef73.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/009ea68342d05d02087c04dae7faaa4e4c1def11.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[azaran](https://hackerone.com/azaran).
This issue was also found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-RTK47OH0).

advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View tag helpers
advisory.description:
### Impact

The fix for
[CVE-2026-33168](https://github.com/rails/rails/security/advisories/GHSA-v55j-83pf-r9cq)
skips blank HTML attribute names in Action View tag helpers, but it tests the
name before converting it to a string. A Symbol name made only of whitespace,
such as `:" "`, is not blank, because `Symbol#blank?` is `Symbol#empty?`, so
it reaches the attribute escaping, which emits an attribute with no name and
produces malformed HTML. The asset tag helpers, such as `image_tag`,
`video_tag` and `audio_tag`, symbolize their options, so a whitespace String
name passed to them takes the same path. A carefully crafted attribute value
could then be misinterpreted by the browser as a separate attribute name,
possibly leading to XSS. Applications that allow users to specify custom HTML
attribute names are affected.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9190210606ffe52f92fdc75637f8ff69404f22c8.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/f47452533e1f28d847c63181b9d5f8b7243ef9a4.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[thepo1es](https://hackerone.com/thepo1es).

advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View strip_tags
advisory.description:
### Impact

`strip_tags` in Action View returns its sanitized output marked `html_safe`,
but the underlying sanitizer encodes only `&`, `<` and `>`, leaving `"` and
`'` unencoded. Because ERB does not escape a string marked `html_safe`,
untrusted input passed through `strip_tags` and rendered inside a quoted HTML
attribute value could close the attribute and add new attributes, possibly
leading to XSS. Applications that render `strip_tags` output from untrusted
input inside an HTML attribute, for example in a `title` attribute or a
`<meta content>` tag, are affected. Output rendered as element content is not
affected.

### Details

`strip_tags` now encodes `"` and `'` in its output, as well as `&`, `<` and
`>`, without double-encoding existing entities. Applications that use
`strip_tags` output outside HTML, such as in a text template or JSON, now see
`"` and `'` where they saw `"` and `'`; `CGI.unescapeHTML` decodes
them. See the Action View CHANGELOG.

### Workarounds

Pass `strip_tags` output to an attribute through a tag helper, which escapes
attribute values, for example `tag.a(title: strip_tags(user_input))`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/568b19cb860322885593e308a7f27aceb779e9d7.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c3772a10f405f9644125cbb484adfd2aa7a25a59.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[lucasluitjes](https://hackerone.com/lucasluitjes).

advisory.title: Possible XSS vulnerability in Action View highlight helper
advisory.description:
### Impact

`ActionView::Helpers::TextHelper#highlight` substitutes each matched phrase
into the `:highlighter` string without escaping it and returns the result
marked HTML-safe. Because sanitizing leaves quote characters in text
unescaped, a match substituted into a quoted attribute value of the
highlighter, such as the `<a href="search?q=\1">` form shown in the method's
documentation, could end the attribute value and add attributes to the
element, possibly leading to XSS. Applications are affected when they pass a
`:highlighter` that places a placeholder inside an attribute value and
highlight text or phrases that a user controls. The default `<mark>\1</mark>`
highlighter and the block form are not affected.

### Details

The fixed releases HTML-escape each group substituted into the `:highlighter`
string, so quotes in a match are rendered as `"` and `'`. Only the
numbered placeholders `\0` to `\9` are expanded; other `String#sub`
replacement escapes, such as `\k<name>`, `\&` and `\\`, are left as written. A
match can no longer begin on the `>` that closes a preceding tag. Escaping
makes a placeholder safe as element content or inside a quoted attribute
value, but not in an unquoted attribute value, a URL, JavaScript or CSS
context, or an attribute whose value is HTML. See the Action View CHANGELOG
for details.

### Workarounds

Use a `:highlighter` that places the matched phrase only in element content,
such as the default `<mark>\1</mark>`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/06938194b4fd59e1d2c8ab4a781f3c1e2b763425.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c796f6198837479ada13290eb8fa767b5219a58a.patch

### Credit

This issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-THHUJQVO).

advisory.title: Rails Active Storage has possible content type bypass via metadata in direct uploads
advisory.description:
### Impact
Active Storage's `DirectUploadsController` accepts arbitrary metadata from the client and persists it on the blob.
Because internal flags like `identified` and `analyzed` are stored in the same metadata hash,
a malicious direct-upload client could set these flags.

### Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

advisory.title: Rails Active Storage has a possible DoS vulnerability when in proxy mode via Range requests
advisory.description:
### Impact
When serving files through Active Storage's `Blobs::ProxyController`,
the controller loads the entire requested byte range into memory before sending it.
A request with a large or unbounded Range header (e.g. `bytes=0-`) could cause the server
to allocate memory proportional to the file size, possibly resulting in a DoS vulnerability through memory exhaustion.

### Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

advisory.title: Rails Active Storage has possible Path Traversal in DiskService
advisory.description:
### Impact
Active Storage's `DiskService#path_for` does not validate that the
resolved filesystem path remains within the storage root directory.
If a blob key containing path traversal sequences (e.g. `../`) is used,
it could allow reading, writing, or deleting arbitrary files on the server.
Blob keys are expected to be trusted strings,
but some applications could be passing user input as keys and would be affected.

### Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

advisory.title: Rails Active Storage has possible glob injection in its DiskService
advisory.description:
### Impact
Active Storage's `DiskService#delete_prefixed` passes blob keys directly to `Dir.glob` without escaping glob metacharacters.
If a blob key contains attacker-controlled input or custom-generated keys with glob metacharacters,
it may be possible to delete unintended files from the storage directory.

### Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

advisory.title: Rails Active Storage has a possible DoS vulnerability in proxy mode via multi-range requests
advisory.description:
## Impact

Active Storage’s proxy controller does not limit the number of byte
ranges in an HTTP Range header. A request with thousands of small
ranges causes disproportionate CPU usage compared to a normal
request for the same file, possibly resulting in a DoS vulnerability.

advisory.title: Possible arbitrary file read and remote code execution in Active Storage variant processing
advisory.description:
## Impact

In its default configuration, a Rails application that displays image
variants may allow an unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary files
from the server, including the process environment. That environment
typically holds secret_key_base and often credentials for external
systems, which may in turn allow escalation to remote code execution
or lateral movement to those systems.

## Affected applications

An application is affected if it meets all of these requirements:

* Uses libvips for Active Storage image processing. This is
  config.active_storage.variant_processor = :vips, which
  load_defaults 7.0 set and no later default has changed.
* Allows image uploads from untrusted users.
  Generating variants is not a separate requirement.

## Workarounds

If libvips < 8.13 is being used, there are no workarounds available
other than removing the dependency on libvips from the application.
Some applications may have ruby-vips declared as a dependency only
for image analysis, and those applications may be able to simply
remove ruby-vips from the Gemfile to remove libvips from the
application. Applications that do not use Active Storage can remove
ruby-vips from the Gemfile to avoid the boot-time checks.

If libvips >= 8.13 is present on the system, applications can disable
the unfuzzed operations without upgrading Rails by setting the
VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED environment variable, which libvips reads while
initializing.

Applications also running ruby-vips >= 2.2.1 or later can instead call
Vips.block_untrusted(true) from an initializer.

## Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by 0xacb, s3np41k1r1t0 and castilho
from Ethiack, and RyotaK from GMO Flatt Security Inc..

advisory.title: Possible local file disclosure in Active Storage video previews and analysis
advisory.description:
### Impact

Active Storage's `VideoPreviewer`, `VideoAnalyzer` and `AudioAnalyzer` run
`ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on a blob's contents without restricting the input
format, so FFmpeg selects a demuxer by probing the file. A blob created
through a direct upload keeps the content type the client declared, so a
client can store an HLS playlist under a `video/*` or `audio/*` type. When
that blob is previewed or analyzed, the `hls` demuxer opens the `file://`
segments that the playlist names, and the preview image or the stored metadata
could disclose a local media file that the application process can read and
whose path the attacker knows.

Applications that accept uploads from untrusted users and generate video
previews, or analyze video or audio attachments with FFmpeg, are affected.

### Details

The fixed releases limit the formats FFmpeg may open to common audio and video
containers, configured by the new
`config.active_storage.ffmpeg_allowed_formats` setting. Files in other formats
no longer preview or receive media metadata; the Active Storage CHANGELOG
names some of them and shows how to add a format to the list.

### Workarounds

Applications that cannot upgrade can stop Active Storage from running FFmpeg
on uploaded files by removing `ActiveStorage::Previewer::VideoPreviewer` from
`config.active_storage.previewers`, and
`ActiveStorage::Analyzer::VideoAnalyzer` and
`ActiveStorage::Analyzer::AudioAnalyzer` from
`config.active_storage.analyzers`.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/3b1f2627538dc597cd973530c08514a26c2b0282.patch
- 8.0:
  https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/69aff80d115bbb9d1e82fd6c6f2fd3ddeafb958b.patch

### Credit

This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher
[w3rmut](https://hackerone.com/w3rmut).

advisory.title: Unsigned Content-Type in Active Storage GCS direct uploads with cache_control
advisory.description:
### Impact

When a GCS service is configured with the `cache_control` option,
`ActiveStorage::Service::GCSService#url_for_direct_upload` signs direct-upload
URLs with V4, and the V4 signature covers only the `Cache-Control` and `Host`
headers. A direct-upload client can therefore send a `Content-Type` of its
choosing, and can omit the declared `Content-MD5`, without invalidating the
URL. GCS stores the supplied content type as object metadata, which takes
precedence over the `response-content-type` that Active Storage sets on
download URLs, so an uploaded object could be served as inline HTML under the
application's bucket path on `storage.googleapis.com`. Script in such an
object runs on the storage origin rather than the application's, but could
register a Service Worker scoped to the bucket path and read or replace a
victim's later responses for signed URLs in that bucket.

Applications that use the GCS service with `cache_control` configured and
accept direct uploads are affected. GCS services without `cache_control` sign
with V2 and are not affected.

### Details

The fixed releases sign every GCS direct-upload URL with V2, which binds an
empty `Content-Type` and the declared `Content-MD5`. The configured
`Cache-Control` is still returned by `headers_for_direct_upload` and sent by
the client, but it is no longer part of the signature, and direct-upload URLs
for these services are no longer limited to V4's seven-day maximum expiry. See
the Active Storage CHANGELOG.

### Workarounds

Removing the `cache_control` option from the GCS service configuration makes
Active Storage sign direct uploads with V2.

### Releases

The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:

### Credit
